source.title: Major Unsolved Problems in Space Plasma Physics

accepted.question_text: In solar-wind magnetohydrodynamic turbulence, why do magnetic-field and velocity-field fluctuation spectra often have a power-law slope close to -5/3, even though the Kolmogorov -5/3 dimensional argument assumes incompressible and isotropic ordinary-fluid turbulence, while the solar wind contains a relatively strong DC magnetic field and Alfvenic turbulence might instead be expected to show a -3/2 slope? Why do density-fluctuation spectra and spectra of fluctuations in the magnetic-field magnitude B also often show -5/3 slopes, and why do some density and magnetic-field-magnitude power spectra flatten at high frequencies while vector magnetic-field and velocity components steepen near the ion-cyclotron dissipation scale?

evidence.quote: Many unsolved issues remain. Why typical spectra of magnetic (or velocity) fluctuations (Matthaeus and Goldstein, 1982) have spectral slopes of ?5/3 is a mystery.
Also puzzling is the fact that spectra of the density fluctuations also have spectral slopes of ?5/3.
the density spectra and the spectra of the fluctuating power in B often show a flattening at high frequencies and that, too, has not been explained.

accepted.question_text: What is the three-dimensional symmetry of interplanetary solar-wind magnetic-field turbulence: are the fluctuations primarily planar, parallel-propagating Alfven waves; quasi-two-dimensional structures with both wave vector and fluctuating magnetic field perpendicular to the background magnetic field; highly refracted waves; pressure-balanced structures; or some mixture of these components?

evidence.quote: It is of fundamental importance to learn the nature of the three-dimensional symmetries of this turbulence because it is the three-dimensional properties that determine how both solar energetic particles and galactic cosmic rays propagate throughout the heliosphere

Whether the fluctuations are truly quasi-two-dimensional in the sense that ?k and ?b are both perpendicular to B (as opposed to, say, being highly refracted waves or pressure-balanced structures) has yet to be determined.

accepted.question_text: How do the three-dimensional structures of interplanetary turbulent magnetic fields determine energetic-particle transport in the heliosphere, including pitch-angle scattering parallel to the background magnetic field, transverse diffusion across magnetic-field lines, stochastic field-line diffusion, whether solar energetic particles from flares and coronal mass ejections reach Earth, and the 22-year modulation of galactic cosmic rays by solar magnetic fields?

evidence.quote: the three-dimensional properties that determine how both solar energetic particles and galactic cosmic rays propagate throughout the heliosphere
Planar, parallel-propagating Alfv?n waves are efficient pitch-angle scatterers (Jokipii, 1971), but only inefficiently transport particles across field lines.
quasi-two-dimensional turbulence causes field lines to diffuse stochastically, which should lead to significant perpendicular diffusion.

accepted.question_text: How should space-plasma models connect the fluid description of inertial-range magnetohydrodynamic turbulence to kinetic physics in the dissipation range, where scales approach the ion Larmor radius or ion skin depth, magnetic reconnection requires at least approximate electron physics, collisionless regions such as the outer heliosphere challenge fluid approximations, and interstellar pickup ions introduce energetically important non-Maxwellian components?

evidence.quote: the dissipation range of the spectrum is poorly studied and poorly understood.

The fluid description used to study inertial range turbulence breaks down as one approaches spatial scales comparable to the ion Larmor radius or ion skin depth and kinetic effects need to be included.
Even at larger scales, fluid descriptions become questionable in regions of space where the plasma becomes collisionless

accepted.question_text: For proton cyclotron waves in low-beta space plasmas, do nonlinear or coarse-grained fluid treatments of resonant wave-particle interaction change the expected damping enough that ion-cyclotron waves in the solar corona may survive longer than linear theory predicts, thereby requiring reevaluation of linear ion-cyclotron damping scenarios?

evidence.quote: Much still needs to be done in this area
ion cyclotron waves may not damp as rapidly as predicted by linear theory.

accepted.question_text: What physical mechanism heats the solar corona from chromospheric temperatures of thousands of kelvin to more than one million kelvin, and how does that mechanism determine the speed and temperature of the solar wind, especially the fast wind above coronal holes, given that fluid models require additional heat sources and proposed mechanisms such as Alfven-wave damping, reconnection events, and velocity filtration each face observational or theoretical constraints?

evidence.quote: Exactly how the corona is heated is not understood
the heating mechanism determines both the speed and temperature of the solar wind, especially the fast wind above coronal holes.
Determining how the corona and solar wind are heated and accelerated continues to be a challenging unsolved problem.

accepted.question_text: For solar flares and coronal mass ejections, what is the geometry of coronal mass ejections and how do they exit the solar corona and evolve into the solar wind? For type II solar radio bursts, where relative to the collisionless shock wave are the electrons accelerated, and where are the fundamental and second-harmonic radio emissions generated?

evidence.quote: One problem at the top of most lists is solar flares and coronal mass ejections (CMEs).
exactly what their geometry is and how they exit from the corona and evolve into the solar wind are still subjects of intense research.
Where in relation to the collisionless shock wave are the electrons accelerated? Where are the fundamental and second harmonic radiation generated?

accepted.question_text: Why do outward-propagating Alfvenic fluctuations in the solar wind evolve and disappear in the outer heliosphere, and what roles do velocity shear, stream interactions, and proximity to the heliospheric current sheet play in that evolution?

evidence.quote: This section illustrates the issue with one complex problem that does appear to have been solved.
outward propagating Alfv?n waves are indicative of turbulence in the solar corona and the interaction of fast and slow wind does stir the solar wind and cause the turbulence to evolve.
velocity shear and proximity to the heliospheric current sheet are critical in the evolution of Alfv?nic fluctuations

needs_review.question_text_raw: Another major puzzle is how to quantitatively describe the interaction of the solar wind with the interstellar medium; a problem probably not amenable to solution using fluid equations.

evidence.quote: Another major puzzle is how to quantitatively describe the interaction of the solar wind with the interstellar medium; a problem probably not amenable to solution using fluid equations.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Certainly no list of unsolved problems would be complete, notwithstanding the graduate student quoted in subsection 1.2, without including magnetospheric substorms.

evidence.quote: Certainly no list of unsolved problems would be complete, notwithstanding the graduate student quoted in subsection 1.2, without including magnetospheric substorms.
